chunks: Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. Ahmad b. al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: al-Husayn b. al-Hasan b. Aban narrated to us from al-Husayn b. Sa'id from Ibn Abi Umayr and Muhammad b. Isma'il from Mansur b. Yunus from Mansur b. Hazim, and Ali b. Isma'il al-Maythami from Mansur b. Hazim, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said:

There is no breastfeeding after weaning. There is no continuous fasting. There is no orphanhood after puberty. There is no silence from day until night. There is no nomadism after the hijra. There is no emigration after the conquest [of Mecca]. There is no divorce before marriage. There is no emancipation before ownership. There is no oath of a child over his father. There is no oath of a slave over his master. There is no oath of a wife over her husband. There is no vow in disobedience [to Allah]. There is no oath in cutting [family] ties.

key_terms.احتلام: Puberty — the age at which a person is no longer considered an orphan in Islamic law
key_terms.تعرب: Nomadism/Arabization — returning to desert Bedouin life after having migrated to the city of the Prophet
key_terms.رضاع: Breastfeeding — in Islamic law, breastfeeding within the first two years establishes a milk-kinship
key_terms.فطام: Weaning — the natural end of breastfeeding, after which milk-kinship cannot be established
key_terms.قطيعة: Cutting ties — severing family relations, which invalidates an oath
key_terms.نذر: Vow (nidhr) — a solemn promise to Allah, invalid if it involves disobedience
key_terms.هجرة: Hijra — emigration from Mecca to Medina; after the conquest, no longer obligatory
key_terms.وصال: Continuous fasting — fasting without breaking at sunset, which is prohibited

ai.seo_question: What are the thirteen legal rulings the Prophet Muhammad stated about breastfeeding, fasting, divorce, oaths and vows?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad enumerates thirteen legal maxims that define the boundaries and preconditions of various Islamic rulings. These concise statements, covering topics from breastfeeding and fasting to oaths and vows, establish foundational jurisprudential principles about the conditions required for legal acts to be valid. This hadith was widely taught by Imam al-Sadiq through the chain of the Imams.
